facts.text: Langhorne got its name in 1876 when the town, then called Attleborough, was renamed for Jeremiah Langhorne, a former Pennsylvania Supreme Court chief justice.
The arrival of the North Pennsylvania Railroad in 1876 sparked a naming dispute between Attleborough and Hulmeville over the station’s name.
The Langhorne Hotel, still operating today, dates back to the 18th century and preserves much of its historic character.
The Lower Trenton Bridge over the Delaware River, a relic of the region’s industrial past, still stands as a landmark in Langhorne.
A 19th‑century canal ran through Langhorne, and its inscription ‘1831 to 1931’ highlights its role in transportation and trade.
Walking through Langhorne, the mix of urban development and historic architecture creates a distinctive streetscape that feels both modern and timeless.
